noun, examples include Eigenname (proper noun), Sammelname (collective noun) and Gattungsname (appellative or common noun). Note: Compounds which aren't hyponyms of substantive are rare and obsolete, like Hauptname or Dingname (substantive noun), Beiname (adjective noun), Fürname (pronoun).
Name.et: From Middle High German name, from Old High German namo, from Proto-West Germanic *namō. Cognate with Dutch naam, Low German Naam, Alemannic German Name, Yiddish נאָמען (nomen), English name, West Frisian namme, Danish navn, Swedish namn.

namesake (person having the same name as another; male or unspecified sex)
namesake (female person having the same name as another)
Namibian (a person from Namibia or of Namibian descent, either male or of unspecified gender)
(the) very same, selfsame (as was mentioned or described previously; either the same object by identity, or sometimes just the same in type or appearance)
Es war das Zimmer, darin Judith Platter während der langen Wintermonate ihre Pflanzen aufbewahrte, die unter ihrer Pflege so herrlich gediehen; das nämliche Zimmer war es, darin sie ihre Vögel hielt.
It was the room wherein Judith Platter kept her plants, which so wondrously prospered under her care, during the long winter months; it was the same room wherein she kept her birds.
namely, specifically; used to further specify what exactly one was talking about just before
Mehr als die Hälfte, nämlich 56%, sehen das kritisch.
More than half, specifically 56%, are critical of it.
because, after all; used to follow up a statement with a second one that justifies the former, treated as a revealing of new information
Ich hab morgen keine Zeit, ich hab nämlich einen Termin.
I don’t have time tomorrow, I have an appointment (because I have an appointment).
name day (feast day of a saint)
a part of speech which can be declined, i.e. substantive, adjective, numeral, article or pronoun
bearer of a name, namesake, person or community of people who share a name
